pr: performance plan PR #1 -- baseline and profiling infrastructure
scope: text-only, open XDNA2 (aie2p) kernels, block prefill route
commit_note: main after PR #213 plus the instrumented tree; the profiling commit is on perf/npu-baseline-profiling

measurement_conditions.npu_pmode: historically requested performance; successful configuration was not independently established
measurement_conditions.load_average: 0.42 at the start of the run, 1.4 over the preceding 5 minutes
measurement_conditions.note: a FIRST pass of these measurements was taken on a box that was both loaded (load average 6.4-10.8) and short of memory (17 GiB free, 12 GiB in swap). Prefill TTFT was 1.6x the historical baseline under those conditions. The numbers in this file are the RE-MEASUREMENT on an idle box, and they reproduce the historical baseline within noise. The first pass is kept in the report as the record of an experiment that was rejected for a measurement reason, not a performance one.

prefill.vs_historical: reproduced within -2.8% to +0.2%; prompt tok/s 6.88 / 7.09 / 7.27 against 6.68 / 7.10 / 7.22
prefill.shape_holds: cost is linear in blocks and flat in the active rows inside a block -- both checks PASS, which is the schedule's own prediction and does not depend on the machine's speed

decode.vs_historical: 2.074 against 2.087 -- reproduced within noise, and flat in prompt length as before

layer_attribution.method: OFLM_OPEN_PROFILE=<path> on the standalone open_qwen36_cli: one JSON row per layer, the columns being differences of the engine's existing StepTiming at the layer boundaries, plus a steady-clock wall per layer
layer_attribution.wall_note: the request total is the model's own timing for one 256-token block; the script's `wall_s` also carries the model load

block_route.widest_layer_note: Layer 0 was the slowest in this single capture; no repeat-based variability conclusion is established.
block_route.residue_definition: outside layer walls; includes lm_head, not the residual of named stage counters

derived.note: the streamed-weight estimate assumes 4.5 bit/packed weight and a linear layer's qkv|z + o + up|gate + down; it is an order-of-magnitude check on where the GEMM time is, not a kernel measurement

variables.OFLM_OPEN_PROFILE: path of a JSONL file; one header, one request and one row per layer. Unset = no hooks run.
variables.OFLM_OPEN_PROFILE_STEPS: how many sequential step() calls to profile (default 8, 0 = block routes only)

records.request: what, tokens, blocks, total_ms, gemm_ms, host_ms, per_token_ms, lmhead_ms, setup_ms, embed_ms, patch_ms, dispatch_ms, layer_wall_ms, residue_ms, layers; what=step is phase-neutral, not a prefill/decode classification
records.layer: what, kind, layer, wall_ms and every StepTiming column that layer moved

instrumentation.overhead_when_enabled: Clock reads at layer boundaries plus JSON serialization/flush; measured over complete ON decode coverage
instrumentation.overhead_when_disabled: one null check per layer boundary (profile_switch)

gates.baseline_reproduced: Historical single-run observations retained; warm-up plus five repeated measurements and variability are still required.
gates.instrumentation_is_free_when_off: PENDING controlled power-mode validation; exploratory parent-OFF/new-OFF medians both 449 ms
gates.instrumentation_changes_no_output: PASS: 16 greedy tokens match between observed block/layer-major routes; eight greedy IDs match every parent/OFF/ON run. This is not an independent numerical oracle.
gates.layer_accounting_balances: PASS: fresh route captures validate all 64 layers per request, route identities and stage nesting; stage-unaccounted time remains explicit
gates.settings_registry: the two new variables are classified in NON_SETTING_ENV_VARS in utilities/generate-registry.py; utilities/scan-settings.py finds both
gates.unit_tests: PASS on review fixes: pytest specs/ 2460 passed, 172 skipped; standalone CTest 4/4; production CTest 29 passed, 2 skipped
gates.enabled_profiling_overhead: PENDING controlled power-mode validation; exploratory new-OFF/new-ON medians both 449 ms, all seven measured decode steps profiled

rejected_experiment.what: the first measurement pass, taken while the box was loaded (load average 6.4-10.8) and short of memory (17 GiB free, 12 GiB swapped out)
rejected_experiment.result: prefill TTFT 62.2 / 118.9 / 234.4 s, i.e. 1.58-1.64x the historical baseline, while decode reproduced at 2.076 tok/s
rejected_experiment.conclusion: the prefill host stages fault and contend for pages under memory pressure while the fully device-bound decode path does not, so the inflation was an environment artefact. Rejected and re-measured on an idle box; the ratios inside a run (GEMM 72% / host 17%, tiling 50% of host) were unchanged between the two passes, which is why they are the figures the next PR is chosen from

not_claimed: any speedup -- this PR is instrumentation only
a GEMM efficiency figure from the kernel side; the 0.60 GB/s and 0.39 TFLOPS here are derived from wall time and assumed weight bytes
anything about vision or long-context attention
limitations: Existing TTFT/rate observations are retained, not new measurements of the corrected tree.
No hardware device timestamps: queue residence, dispatch execution and idle time remain unresolved.
The rejected first-pass slowdown correlates with load/memory pressure; page faults were not measured to prove causation.
